celebrity.full_text_en:
5 Levels of AI agent autonomy (and who owns what?):

The right level isn't set by how capable the model is.

It's set by what a wrong action would cost.

𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟭: 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿
↳ The agent acts only when you ask: a query, an edit, a draft.
↳ You own: every decision and every step.

𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟮: 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿
↳ You and the agent plan and execute together, passing control back and forth.
↳ You own: the plan, and when to take the wheel.

𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟯: 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁
↳ The agent leads the task and checks in for your expertise or preferences.
↳ You own: the context and judgement it can't find on its own.

𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟰: 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿
↳ The agent works on its own and stops for sign-off on risky actions: a migration, a deploy, a customer email.
↳ You own: the line between routine and risky, and the final yes.

𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟱: 𝗢𝗯𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗲𝗿
↳ The agent runs end to end while you monitor.
↳ You own: the goal, the limits, and the stop button.

Before moving an agent up a level:

→ Can its actions be undone?
→ Is every action logged?
→ Would you spot a wrong one within minutes?

Those checks keep an agent safe. They don't show whether all the work, human and AI, still matches the plan.

Tempo Loop checks that continuously. It connects to the tools you already use, starting with Jira, and compares time, capacity and spend against the strategy that funded the work. When something drifts, it recommends a fix with its tradeoffs while there's still time to act.

As with your agents, the decision stays with people: your team approves the fix, and Loop orchestrates it back into those tools. Human and AI work are governed in one system.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Added this section from @X's own rules

Most people don't know that AI reply bots are explicitly not permitted to run on here

And duplicate pasting the same reply with automation is the same thing

X has an entire page dedicated to it

The reason for the "Let's connect 🤝" reply spam is simple, people run automated bots (or do it manually) so that when they get a reply with connect in it, they follow the person and that person automatically follows them too

That way they both get 1 new follower, and that brings them closer to the minimum of 500 verified followers to get accepted into X's Monetization program

Before reply spamming paid you good money: about $10 per million views, so they scripted that and auto replied and they made money. But @X killed that in January this year. Now only timeline views pay you money

Also you need 500,000 impressions in the last 3 months (~166,000 per month) to get into X's Monetization Program, so the idea is to pump replies/posts too such a high level that you force these amounts of views

Now the scheme is to grow an account to a few thousand followers, then sell it, or use it for paid product placements, crypto pump and dumps or AI apps/tools

A large part of spam comes from poor countries where just making $100/mo more from X makes a big difference, so I get it, but I think we should also actively fight it because reply spam is destroying this platform and then people will just leave and I don't like that

I made so many friends on here over the last decade and want to continue doing so, if most of my interactions on here are with spam bots, I won't be able to do that anymore!

celebrity.title_zh:
一个棘手的LLM面试问题：

您将 LLM 转移到更快的 GPU。

分析证实其内核现在完成得更快，但生成令牌之间的时间几乎没有变化。

模型、精度和批量大小相同。

预期的加速哪里去了？

（答案如下）

LLM 前向传递并不是一项巨大的
celebrity.author: @DailyDoseOfDS_
celebrity.summary_zh:
GPU 操作。

它启动一系列操作来进行注意力、矩阵相乘、标准化、采样、数据移动和其他工作。

如果没有 CUDA Graph，CPU 会单独准备并提交这些操作。

每次启动仅增加少量开销，但逐个令牌解码会对每个生成的令牌重复类似的序列。

这造成了一个奇怪的瓶颈。

有些内核只需几微秒即可完成。 GPU 可以在 CPU 提交下一个内核之前完成一个内核。

这会在探查器跟踪中留下空白空间。这些差距不是模型计算。它们显示 GPU 正在等待下一个操作。

CUDA Graph 改变了这项工作到达 GPU 的方式。

运行时捕获一次可重复的操作序列，包括它们的依赖项。稍后的迭代通过一个图启动重放捕获的序列，而不是单独提交每个操作。

需要明确的是，内核本身并没有变得更快。

此外，模型不会变小，并且前向传递执行几乎相同的计算。

大部分收益来自于消除内核之间的 CPU 启动工作。

这在 LLM 解码期间特别有用。

每个解码步骤为每个序列处理一个新标记。这会产生许多短的、重复的 GPU 操作，其中启动开销可能成为总延迟的一个有意义的部分。

预填充通常表现不同。

较大的提示可以让 GPU 进行更多并行工作，从而生成运行时间更长的内核。当这些内核已经让 GPU 忙碌时，减少启动开销就不那么重要了。

还有一个权衡。

捕获的图在每次重放时都需要相同的内核序列、稳定的参数、固定的内存地址和兼容的执行结构。

推理服务器可处理不同的批量大小以及不同的预填充、混合和解码工作负载。一张捕获的图无法有效覆盖每条执行路径。

因此，vLLM 和 TensorRT-LLM 等引擎可以捕获几种常见执行情况和批量大小的图表。

当实时批次与捕获的大小不匹配时，引擎可以使用急切执行或将批次填充到捕获的大小。

捕获更多尺寸可以提高图形覆盖范围，但也会消耗更多 GPU 内存并增加启动时间。

因此 CUDA Graph 并不是通用的推理速度开关。

他们以灵活性和设置成本为代价换取较低的稳态启动开销。

下图显示了核心机制。

- 如果没有图表，CPU 会独立提交每个内核，并且可能会在 GPU 时间线上留下空闲间隙。
- 通过图表，序列被捕获一次并作为一个单元重播。

CUDA 图是为什么 LLM 推理需要专门的服务引擎而不是标准预测 API 的一个例子。

我们之前解释了传统 ML 推理和 LLM 推理之间的五个架构差异。

请阅读下面的内容。
celebrity.full_text_en:
A tricky LLM interview question:

You move your LLM to a faster GPU.

Profiling confirms its kernels now finish sooner, but the time between generated tokens barely changes.

The model, precision, and batch size are identical.

Where did the expected speedup go?

(answer below)

An LLM forward pass is not one giant GPU operation.

It launches a sequence of operations for attention, matmul, normalization, sampling, data movement, and other work.

Without CUDA Graphs, the CPU prepares and submits these operations individually.

Each launch adds only a small amount of overhead, but token-by-token decoding repeats a similar sequence for every generated token.

This creates a strange bottleneck.

Some kernels finish in only a few microseconds. The GPU can complete one kernel before the CPU has submitted the next one.

That leaves empty spaces in a profiler trace. These gaps are not model computation. They show the GPU waiting for its next operation.

CUDA Graphs change how this work reaches the GPU.

The runtime captures a repeatable sequence of operations once, including their dependencies. Later iterations replay the captured sequence through one graph launch instead of submitting every operation separately.

To be clear, the kernels themselves do not become substantially faster.

Also, the model does not get smaller, and the forward pass performs almost the same computation.

Most of the gain comes from removing CPU launch work between kernels.

This is especially useful during LLM decoding.

Each decoding step processes one new token per sequence. This produces many short, repeated GPU operations where launch overhead can become a meaningful part of total latency.

Prefill often behaves differently.

A large prompt gives the GPU more parallel work, producing longer-running kernels. When those kernels already keep the GPU busy, reducing launch overhead matters less.

There is also a tradeoff.

A captured graph expects the same kernel sequence, stable arguments, fixed memory addresses, and a compatible execution structure on every replay.

Inference servers handle varying batch sizes and different prefill, mixed, and decode workloads. One captured graph cannot cover every execution path efficiently.

Engines such as vLLM and TensorRT-LLM therefore capture graphs for several common execution cases and batch sizes.

When a live batch does not match a captured size, the engine may use eager execution or pad the batch to a captured size.

Capturing more sizes improves graph coverage, but it also consumes more GPU memory and increases startup time.

So CUDA Graphs are not a universal inference speed switch.

They trade flexibility and setup cost for lower steady-state launch overhead.

The visual below shows the core mechanism.

- Without a graph, the CPU submits each kernel independently and may leave idle gaps on the GPU timeline.
- With a graph, the sequence is captured once and replayed as a unit.

CUDA Graphs are one example of why LLM inference needs a specialized serving engine rather than a standard prediction API.

We previously explained five architectural differences between traditional ML inference and LLM inference.

Read it below.

celebrity.summary_zh:
iv 和社交媒体的步伐成为关键。

现在我们使用的工具每月或每周都在变化。我正在跟踪前沿人工智能模型的发展，而不仅仅是我的领域。我的电子邮件收件箱也仍然在那里。斯莱克也是如此。我发现我的注意力在我的职业生涯中比以往任何时候都更加分散。

从某种客观的“产出”衡量标准来看，我现在的工作效率肯定比以往任何时候都高。但我的感觉并不是一种更多的成就感。相反，情况恰恰相反。我有一种无限的可能性和快速进步的紧迫感。尚未实现的潜力总是会让一个人已经完成的事情相形见绌。

我是否只需要更多组织得更好的代理？我不这么认为。我对所有旨在提高生产力的技术的经验是，它不会减少我们的工作或压力。它只是堆积了更多我们可以而且应该做的事情。

这也可能是我职业生涯中最激动人心的时刻——也许兴奋和压力是并存的。当我弄清楚如何驾驭新世界时，我会告诉你。就在我清空收件箱后......
celebrity.full_text_en:
It feels like a lifetime ago when my big work stress was keeping up with email.  

Every decade or so, there would be a major change in the field and the tools we used. One could adapt. 

Then my field (computer vision) grew by an order of magnitude and papers started appearing on arXiv every week and then every day. Keeping up with arXiv and social media became key. 

Now the tools we use are changing monthly or weekly. I'm tracking developments in frontier AI models and not just my field. My email inbox is still there too. So is Slack. I find my attention is more fragmented than ever before in my career. 

I'm definitely more productive now than ever before, by some objective measure of "output". But the feeling I have is not one of more accomplishment. Instead, it's rather the opposite. I have a feeling of limitless possibility and an urgency to make rapid progress. The unfulfilled potential of that will always dwarf what one has already done. 

Do I just need more agents that are better organized? I don't think so. My experience with all technology that is supposed to improve our productivity is that it does not reduce our work or our stress. It just piles on more things that we can and should do.

This is also probably the most exciting time in my career -- maybe excitement and stress go together. When I figure out how to navigate the new world, I'll let you know. Right after I clear out my inbox....

然后我的领域（计算机视觉）增长了一个数量级，论文开始每周出现在 arXiv 上，然后是每天。跟上 arXiv 和社交媒体的步伐成为关键。

现在我们使用的工具每月或每周都在变化。我正在跟踪前沿人工智能模型的发展，而不仅仅是我的领域。我的电子邮件收件箱也仍然在那里。斯莱克也是如此。我发现我的注意力在我的职业生涯中比以往任何时候都更加分散。

从某种客观的“产出”衡量标准来看，我现在的工作效率肯定比以往任何时候都高。但我的感觉并不是一种更多的成就感。相反，情况恰恰相反。我有一种无限的可能性和快速进步的紧迫感。尚未实现的潜力总是会让一个人已经完成的事情相形见绌。

我是否只需要更多组织得更好的代理？我不这么认为。我对所有旨在提高生产力的技术的经验是，它不会减少我们的工作或压力。它只是堆积了更多我们可以而且应该做的事情。

这也可能是我职业生涯中最激动人心的时刻——也许兴奋和压力是并存的。当我弄清楚如何驾驭新世界时，我会告诉你。就在我清空收件箱后......

prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
prompts.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一位兼具应用数学博士学位与顶级深度学习框架优化经验的算法工程师。请将以下论文中的 LaTeX 数学公式翻译为高质量的 PyTorch 实现：
1. 逐一解释公式中各标量、向量与张量上下标的精确几何与物理含义；
2. 编写无 Python 原生 for 循环的高性能向量化代码（善用 torch.einsum, bmm, 或 broadcast 广播机制）；
3. 在每行关键张量操作后标注显式的 Shape 注释（如 `# [Batch, Heads, Seq_Len, Dim]`），并加入数值稳定性保护（如防除以零的 eps 与 log-sum-exp 技巧）。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本

- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

prompts.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""

Gavin Baker 表示，Grok Bot 感觉就像又一个 ChatGPT 时刻，因为它将数小时的 Claude Code 工作变成了几秒钟：

“你看看这些 23 岁的孩子，他们使用人工智能的方式非常流畅，而且很自然。我只是觉得，也许在某种程度上，无论我多么努力，我都永远不会做到，而且我真的很努力。”

“我们有了 Claude Code。我构建了一些东西，做了一些很酷的东西，而且，我不知道，在创建 Grok Bots 的 3 分钟内，我对我创建的所有东西都有了更好的版本。”

“我喜欢播客摘要生成器……在 Grok Bot 中只需 10 秒。太棒了，而且太棒了。”

“一个 Substack 总结器、一个 X 总结器、一个针对主题和股票的 X 情绪跟踪器……所有这些都需要我使用 Claude Code 来工作几个小时，而使用 Grok Bot 则需要花费 7 到 12 秒的时间。而且它更好。”

“对我来说，Grok Bot 确实感觉像是另一个 ChatGPT 时刻。”

@GavinSBaker @DavidGeorge83
viral_posts.full_text_en:
Gavin Baker says Grok Bot feels like another ChatGPT moment because it turns hours of Claude Code work into seconds:

"You see these 23-year-old kids and just the way they use AI, they're just fluent and native in it. I just feel like maybe in a way that no matter how hard I try, I will never be, and I'm trying really hard."

"We got Claude Code. I built some stuff, did some cool stuff, and in, I don't know, 3 minutes of creating Grok Bots, I had much better versions of everything I created."

"I love having a podcast summarizer... It takes 10 seconds in Grok Bot. It's amazing, and it's so good."

"A Substack summarizer, an X summarizer, an X sentiment tracker for topics and stocks... All of those would have taken me hours working with Claude Code, and they each took 7 to 12 seconds with Grok Bot. And it's better."

"To me, Grok Bot does feel like another ChatGPT moment."

viral_posts.full_text_zh:
T3 代码/Theo 收据#21：

谷歌介入了。

两天前，当用户通过 T3 Code 连接后几分钟内就被禁止付费 Google Antigravity 帐户时，官方常见问题解答仍然承诺：T3 Code 属于 Claude Code、Codex 和 Google Antigravity 的 TOS 范围内……如果它在 T3 Code 中运行，您可以相信它是安全的。

当被禁止的用户打开问题 #40713 和问题 #41536 时，维护者否认调用 Antigravity 的后端或重复使用代币，Theo 将第三方代理归咎于 X，并且在 3 分钟内被禁止的新 20 美元帐户被作为重复帐户关闭，对用户的警告为零。

不到 48 小时后，T3 维护者自己的两个合并 PR 炸毁了整个防御。

首先，核心维护者 Julius 在 PR #43026（世界标准时间 11 月 25 日合并）中明确承认：

Antigravity 仅支持外部客户端的 ACP。 Google 告诉我们，调用其内部 API 可能会标记帐户。

PR 机构继续承认 T3 Code 在两个不同的地方（本地提供商探针和内置 CLIProxyAPI 中心读取器）攻击 Google 的内部 http://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com 端点（retrieveUserQuotaSummary / fetchAvailableModels），并补充说：任何一个都可能给用户带来麻烦。

然后，它会直接删除 antigravityUsageLimits.ts — 执行配额探测、OAuth 刷新、macOS 密钥环/Windows 凭据存储读取和欺骗 antigravity/hub 用户代理的确切文件 — 并从应用程序/服务器中删除 @napi-rs/keyring。

然后是 PR #43087（于 UTC 时间 11 月 26 日合并），承认了第二个欺骗技巧：

在 agy 1.5.0 上，或每当 T3 无法读取运行时版本时，Antigravity ACP 握手会发送 clientInfo: { name: zed, version: 0.0.0 } 来模拟列入白名单的编辑器 Zed 并解锁 Claude 和 GPT 模型。 PR 明确写道：冒充另一个客户违反了同样的规则。直到现在，T3 才识别为 t3 代码并拒绝 agy 1.5.0。

v0.1.13 几小时前发布时是如何披露所有这些的？

T3 Code / Theo Receipt #21:

Google stepped in.

Two days ago, when users got their paid Google Antigravity accounts banned within minutes of connecting them through T3 Code, the official FAQ still promised: T3 Code is within the TOS of Claude Code, Codex, and Google Antigravity... If it works in T3 Code, you can trust it is safe.

When banned users opened Issue #40713 and Issue #41536, maintainers denied calling Antigravity's backend or reusing tokens, Theo blamed third-party proxies on X, and a fresh $20 account banned in 3 minutes was closed as a duplicate with zero warning to users.

Less than 48 hours later, two merged PRs from the T3 maintainers themselves blew up that entire defense.

First, PR #43026 (merged Nov 25 UTC) by core maintainer Julius opens with this exact admission:

Antigravity supports only ACP for external clients. Google told us that calling its internal APIs can get an account flagged.

The PR body goes on to admit T3 Code was hitting Google's internal http://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com endpoints (retrieveUserQuotaSummary / fetchAvailableModels) in two separate places — the local provider probe and the built-in CLIProxyAPI hub reader — adding: Either one could get users in trouble.

It then deletes antigravityUsageLimits.ts outright — the exact file doing the quota probe, OAuth refresh, macOS keyring / Windows credential store reads, and spoofed antigravity/hub User-Agent — and drops @napi-rs/keyring from apps/server.

Then came PR #43087 (merged Nov 26 UTC), admitting a second spoofing trick:

On agy 1.5.0, or whenever T3 couldn't read the runtime version, the Antigravity ACP handshake sent clientInfo: { name: zed, version: 0.0.0 } to impersonate allowlisted editor Zed and unlock Claude and GPT models. The PR explicitly writes: Posing as another client breaks the same rule. Only now does T3 identify as t3-code and reject agy 1.5.0.

And how did v0.1.13 disclose all of this when it shipped hours ago?

Across 401 changes, the 7 human-written highlights cover GBK text files, copying file paths, and stopping simulators. Zero mention of Google's ban warning, zero mention of stripping internal API probes, zero mention of impersonating Zed — all buried inside Plus 380 more bug fixes and performance improvements.

The repo now sits at 81,000+ stars and still has 0 GitHub Security Advisories. Paid Google accounts banned after trusting the FAQ's safe guarantee got neither an advisory nor an apology.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Software engineering skills and fundamentals will be even more valuable in the age of AI-powered software engineering. I'm seeing this happen in real time.

A lot of vibe coders are discovering the basics of software engineering through trial and error. For example, I've seen several of my non-coder friends learn "feature creep" through experience. 

When all it takes to add a feature is to prompt Claude Code or Codex to "add X," it all seems easy. But then, when features pile up on each other and your code slows to a crawl to the point that even the AI agent can't make sense of what is going on, then you begin to think, "Hmmm... maybe those software engineers know a few things that are worth learning."

Stick to the fundamentals, know your value and the value of the experience you've accrued over the years.
